about.title: Tustin Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Most people who fall in Tustin do not think of it as a legal matter at first. You pick yourself up in a grocery aisle off Red Hill Avenue, feel embarrassed, and only later realize your wrist or back is not right. Premises liability law in California is built around one question: did the owner know, or should they have known, about the hazard and fail to fix it or warn you? That is called notice, and it is where these claims are won or lost. Tustin is a city of about 80,000 people spread across shopping centers, office parks near Jamboree Road, and older residential blocks, so falls happen in every kind of setting. Video from a store or parking structure is often erased within days, which makes early action matter. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that introduces you to an independent attorney in our network. Those attorneys work on contingency, so you owe no fee unless your claim results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Tustin Residents Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Attorneys who focus on proving notice
items.desc: California requires you to show the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. The attorneys we connect you with know how to gather inspection logs, maintenance records, and witness accounts that speak to that point.

items.title: Help preserving video before it disappears
items.desc: Surveillance footage from a Tustin store or parking lot is routinely overwritten. An attorney can send a preservation demand quickly so the evidence of what you slipped on does not vanish.

items.title: Deadlines handled, fault questions answered
items.desc: You generally have two years to file, but far less if a public entity owns the property. And because California uses pure comparative fault, being partly blamed for a fall does not end your claim; an attorney can explain how that math works for your situation.

items.question: I fell on a city sidewalk in Tustin. Is the deadline different?
items.answer: Yes, and this catches many people off guard. When the property belongs to a public entity such as the City of Tustin or Orange County, you typically must file a formal government claim within six months, well ahead of the two-year deadline that applies to private owners. Missing that window can end the case before it starts. Getting an attorney involved early protects that timeline.

items.question: The store says I should have been watching where I was walking. Does that mean I have no case?
items.answer: Not under California law. The state follows pure comparative fault, which means your recovery can be reduced by your share of responsibility rather than eliminated. If a jury found you 20 percent at fault, for example, you could still recover the other 80 percent. An attorney can weigh how the facts of your fall fit that framework.

items.question: What should I do right now if I fell at a Tustin business?
items.answer: Photograph the exact spot, the hazard, and your footwear before anything is cleaned up or moved. Ask the manager to write an incident report and request that surveillance video be saved. See a doctor even if you feel mostly fine, since falls often produce symptoms a day or two later. Then reach out to us and we will connect you with an attorney for free.
